claim: Grab-and-drag stretches the surface toward the cursor like elastic skin pinned at its corners, snapping back with a wobble on release. The card texture/chrome stays intact through the stretch.

q1_defects.answer: No blocking defects. The real card (brass/gold header bar, blue accent dot top-right, three grey content rows) is preserved and distorted as a cohesive elastic skin in every frame — NOT a featureless placeholder slab. Card content stays tack-sharp at native resolution; brass and rows hold crisp edges through the warp. No clipping, no broken frames, no console/network errors (metrics: consoleErrors=[], networkErrors=[], backend=webgpu). One non-blocking issue: the wobble control is pixel-identical across low/mid/high (metrics: wobble pixelDiff meanAbsDiff=0, changedFrac=0, changed=false), but this is a static-pin capture artifact — wobble governs the post-release snap-back oscillation, which has nothing to act on while the surface is frozen mid-hold (stimulus.controlsPinT=1).
evidence: metrics: wobble pixelDiff meanAbsDiff=0 changedFrac=0 changed=false (frozen-mid-hold pin)

q2_reads_as.answer: Yes, at premium quality. The deformation reads unmistakably as an elastic-skin stretch pinned at the corners: play-1 begins the rightward pull/bow, play-2 shows a deep curved wave where header and rows bend toward the drag point while corners stay anchored, play-3 shows the ease-back/wobble relaxation. grabStrength-high delivers a pronounced deep stretch. The motion is organic and physically plausible, clearly outclassing flat DOM filter effects.

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes. idle.png shows a clean, fully legible card that invites a grab; the play frames make the stretch obvious and dramatic. The effect is large-amplitude and the named knob is 'Grab Strength', matching the grab-and-drag mental model.

q4_responsive.answer: 3 of 4 controls are dramatically live. grabStrength low is nearly flat vs high showing a deep elastic pull (metrics: meanAbsDiff=6.86, changedFrac=0.11). falloff-low is a tight localized V-pinch vs falloff-high a broad full-width bow (metrics: meanAbsDiff=8.28, changedFrac=0.12). stiffness-low is a gentle even bow vs stiffness-high a deep saggy drag (metrics: meanAbsDiff=9.38, changedFrac=0.14). The wobble control shows zero delta (metrics: meanAbsDiff=0) — a static-pin capture limitation since wobble only animates the release oscillation, not the held deformation shown in the pinned frame.
evidence: metrics: grabStrength changed=true / falloff changed=true / stiffness changed=true / wobble changed=false

q5_net.answer: PLEASED. A premium, texture-preserving elastic-warp that reads exactly as its claim, keeps the real card chrome sharp and intact through a large organic deformation, and exposes three strongly responsive controls. The only blemish is the wobble control showing no delta in the frozen capture — a known harness artifact (release-oscillation params have nothing to act on during a held mid-drag pin), so it is a non-blocking flag rather than a defect.

flags.note: The 'wobble' control is pixel-identical across low/mid/high in the captured frames (dead in this capture). This is almost certainly a static-pin artifact — wobble governs the post-release snap-back oscillation, which cannot be observed in a frame frozen mid-hold (stimulus.controlsPinT=1). Recommend a release-phase capture (a frame sampled shortly after pointer-up) to confirm wobble is genuinely live; if it remains dead under a release-phase pin, escalate to mustFix.
flags.evidence: metrics: wobble pixelDiff meanAbsDiff=0 changedFrac=0 changed=false; control-wobble-low.png and control-wobble-high.png are visually identical

flags.note: At the deepest warps (stiffness-high, grabStrength-high) the three grey rows merge into broad dark masses and lose individual separation. This reads as intentional extreme stretch rather than blur, but a touch more inter-row contrast preservation at peak amplitude would feel even more premium. Pure taste.
